objects.original: A Riemannian submanifold M of Euclidean E, intrinsic f and ambient extension f-bar, with tangent spaces T_x M.
objects.reconstructed: A real Hilbert E, complete linear subspace K, ambient function f, shift a, point u in K and representing vector g; F(v)=f(a+v).
objects.evidence: The source has intrinsic and extrinsic objects. The Lean declaration has no manifold, tangent bundle, intrinsic differential, or extension-agreement predicate; its K is a Submodule and its restricted function is a literal composition.

domains.original: Finite-dimensional E; generally nonlinear M; f-bar is defined on a neighborhood of M.
domains.reconstructed: Possibly infinite-dimensional complete real inner-product E; complete K; total f:E→ℝ; restriction on all K.
domains.evidence: Scoped Lean parameters expose CompleteSpace E and CompleteSpace K without FiniteDimensional; the domain is the affine parameter space. This is broader in dimension and narrower in geometry, not equivalent domains. Neighborhood extensions need a separate locality adapter.

quantifiers.original: For every manifold point and any smooth neighborhood extension, the same intrinsic gradient is obtained.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every admissible E,K,f,a,g,u, a pointwise HasGradientAt premise implies HasGradientAt for the literal affine restriction at u.
quantifiers.evidence: Universality over u does not supply the source quantification over intrinsic functions and their agreeing extensions. There is no statement comparing extensions or identifying derivatives through a nonlinear manifold inclusion.

assumptions.original: Smooth f and extension; M has the induced Riemannian metric.
assumptions.reconstructed: E and K are complete real inner-product spaces, with inherited K metric; only ambient HasGradientAt f g (a+u) is required.
assumptions.evidence: Finite-dimensional source spaces are complete automatically; the Lean completeness binders support Riesz identification and projector existence in the Hilbert generalization. HasGradientAt means HasFDerivAt with toDual g, not a totalized gradient equality. No restriction derivative is assumed. Pointwise regularity is weaker than smoothness, legitimately declared for this prerequisite.

conclusion.original: The manifold gradient equals tangent projection of the extension gradient.
conclusion.reconstructed: The affine restriction has genuine gradient K.orthogonalProjectionOnto g, a vector typed in K.
conclusion.evidence: The projection identity has the same mathematical shape after the affine specialization, but the reconstructed theorem cannot prove the full nonlinear manifold statement. It neither constructs the intrinsic gradient field nor verifies the nonlinear differential adapter or extension independence.

scopes.original: Riemannian gradients as an intrinsic vector field; source metric pairing uses the tangent metric.
scopes.reconstructed: A pointwise Hilbert-space gradient predicate, inherited metric and direction-space projection; a is a point shift.
scopes.evidence: Real inner-product symmetry reconciles pairing order. The projected vector is not a+P_K g. Source field smoothness is outside this declaration and, more precisely, is a subsequent Exercise3.66 rather than an explicit extra conclusion in Prop3.61. The publication correctly leaves smooth-field and nonlinear-differential obligations unbound.

constant_dependencies.original: No numerical constants or rates occur in the projection identity.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: No numerical constants or rates; dependence is on E,K,f,a,g,u and inherited inner products.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The Lean result has no dimensional factors, regularity constants, positive parameters, or metric rescaling. Normalization and induced metric agree in the declared affine boundary.

deltas.description: Nonlinear manifolds and intrinsic differentials are absent. This blocks equivalence to full Prop3.61, but does not invalidate the explicitly declared affine-gradient prerequisite.
Hilbert ambient/complete K generalize finite dimensions, while affine restriction specializes geometry. The candidate explicitly discloses both; neither is a proposed correction of Boumal.

No intrinsic function/extension-agreement or extension-independence quantifier is formalized. Full source coverage remains pending; an arbitrary total ambient f and its literal restriction do not silently close this obligation.

Pointwise genuine Fréchet differentiability replaces smoothness for the affine prerequisite. Completeness is explicit for the Hilbert setting and automatic in the finite-dimensional specialization; it is not an excess source hypothesis claimed for Prop3.61.
The conclusion proves the affine restriction gradient only. The binding role=prerequisite and supports=[affine-gradient] are honest; a proof-edge or exact/full-source-completion badge would be false.

No smooth gradient field is proved. That source development belongs to Exercise3.66 beyond the Prop3.61 projection formula. The candidate correctly retains its smooth-field obligation and makes a pointwise claim only.
